pairs.subject: measurement-honesty
pairs.evidence: lib/civic/votes.ts:25 partyDiscipline derives a percentage over `present` members with no floor beyond present===0, so a party with one or two members present renders 100 % / 50 % discipline (to 0.1 p.b. in disciplineByParty) on ChamberDetail and DisciplineBoard — a rate one extra vote can swing across any band.

techniques.evidence: lib/civic/votes.ts:25 Only floor is present>0 (line 24); no declared minimum sample, and the result is rounded to 0.1 % (line 56) regardless of denominator — precision the sample cannot support.

lib/civic/votes.ts:24 No-one-present returns null instead of the old fabricated 1 (100 %); test data.test.ts:189-192 pins it, and registry.ts czechTileNumber refuses non-numeric tiles rather than imputing 0.

lib/civic/votes.ts:58 Average divides by measured roll calls only and emits null when none were measured; perRc with its nulls travels beside avg as the subset disclosure (avg itself carries no measured count).
lib/civic/data.test.ts:235 Tests assert co-published parts sum to wholes: histogram vs row count, party splits vs seats and chamber totals (160-164), the avg tile vs CHAMBER_SUMMARY (240-243).
